transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-24
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Evan Marshall (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Marcus Yao (Redwood Solutions), Tom Alvarez (HarborPay Legal), Hannah Li (HarborPay Procurement), Jorge Ramos (HarborPay InfoSec), Maya Chen (HarborPay Platform)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Readout focused on commercial terms (MSA/DPA redlines), initial SLA thresholds, and security questions around KMS/SSO/VPC and on-prem options.
- Agreement on pilot: 3-week bench with Dedicated pool + canary routing, subject to SLA and billing path approval.
- Next steps: redline exchange, perf/cost spreadsheet, security Q&A, and scheduling technical deep dive.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and indemnity/limit language
- DPA/data residency and retention windows
- SLA targets (p95 latency, uptime) and remediation credits
- Pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted modes, burst/overage handling
- KMS/HSM, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and network connectivity (VPC peering vs Private deployment)

Action items (auto-section): see metadata action_items for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan M: ok hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll do a quick readout from the onboarding working group, the goal is to align legal/commercial and security so we can start pilot next week if possible.
[00:14] Tom A (HarborPay): thanks Evan, yes legal here, we have a few redlines on the MSA around liability cap and data processing clauses, also want clar clarity on sub processors.
[00:26] Priya S: understood, on the sub-processor side Redwood has a list we can share, and for Dedicated we can commit to limited subprocessors for the pilot — we'll note that in the doc.
[00:40] Hannah L: procurement chiming in — pricing question: is there a separate monthly minimum for Dedicated? how are burst overages billed?
[00:52] Marcus Y: quick answer, Dedicated has a baseline reservation + burst pool; billing is split into reserved monthly commit and usage for bursts, we'll send a sample bill.
[01:05] Jorge R: from InfoSec: need to validate KMS flow — can Redwood integrate with our HSM or do we have to use Redwood KMS? also egress controls and audit log retention.
[01:18] Priya S: short answer, we support customer-managed KMS via standard envelope encryption and can work with partner HSMs, though on-prem HSM integrations sometimes need additional engineering time — we can scope that in the tech deep-dive. logging retention is configurable but we'll note the default retention is 90 days unless extended.
[01:35] Tom A: on the DPA, HarborPay requires data residency EU for EU customers; can Redwood guarantee region pinning for models and logs?
[01:47] Evan M: yes region pinning is possible for Private or Dedicated in our EU region; hosted has more limited guarantees. For the pilot we can stand up Dedicated in eu-west-1 to meet residency.
[02:01] Maya C: quick note, we need KV cache behavior spelled out — if we do prefix caching, does cached data leave our VPC? this is a concern for PII.
[02:14] Priya S: good point, prefix/KV caching is in-memory within the serving runtime, it doesn't persist to object storage unless the customer opts in; for Dedicated + VPC we can ensure cache stays within the tenant boundary. I'll follow up with the architecture diagram.
[02:31] Hannah L: circling back to pricing — can you provide a per-token estimate for the pilot and for projected monthly usage of ~200M tokens? we need that for our FinOps review.
[02:44] Marcus Y: yes we'll produce a pro-forma. important to note quantization and batching changes cost; we'll show a range: hosted cheaper per-token at low volumes, Dedicated becomes more economical at scale.
[02:58] Jorge R: another question on SSO - we use SAML + Okta, do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
[03:07] Evan M: yes SAML SSO is supported and SCIM provisioning is available under enterprise plans, will require a little config during onboarding.
[03:20] Tom A: legal redlines — our counsel asked for a $5M liability cap and carveouts for gross negligence; does Redwood have standard language?
[03:32] Evan M: our standard is a $2M cap for SMB, but for enterprise we can negotiate; often we do higher caps in exchange for commensurate insurance updates. we can get internal approval for $5M with procurement terms.
[03:48] Tom A: ok we'll share the redline.
[03:51] Priya S: technical caveat: the SLA target for p95 latency depends on sequence length and model family; for 1k token sequences we typically see higher p95. For the pilot we should define a representative prompt set so SLAs are realistic.
[04:06] Maya C: yes we can share a prompt set and sample QPS.
[04:12] Priya S: perfect — we'll need that to size the Dedicated pool.
[04:18] Jorge R: on audit logs: retention plus integrity — we need tamper evidence and long-term retention for 7 years for certain transactions, can that be exported to our object store?
[04:30] Evan M: we can provide audit log streaming to S3/GCS and sign them; long-term retention export is possible with retention policy configs. may need extra cost.
[04:42] Hannah L: procurement asks about billing path: is it monthly invoiced via Redwood or do you do marketplace? we have preference for invoiced.
[04:53] Evan M: Redwood supports direct invoicing with Net 30 terms for enterprise contracts, marketplace options exist but invoiced is fine.
[05:02] Hannah L: pending internal approvals, we'll likely ask for Net 45 — is that flexible?
[05:10] Evan M: Net 45 will need sales manager approval; we'll flag that as part of the commercial terms.
[05:18] Tom A: anything about export controls? we operate in regulated verticals — need to ensure no restricted tech flow.
[05:26] Priya S: we have export control clauses and can do contractual assurances; for private deployments we can offer on-prem for restricted workloads.
[05:35] Marcus Y: also worth calling out fallback routing — if Dedicated capacity is saturated, we can route to a compatible model in a different capacity tier. that's usually a contract-level behavior: do you allow fallback?
[05:49] Maya C: we prefer no external fallback for regulated traffic, but for non-sensitive paths fallback is OK. we should mark which API routes are allowed to fallback.
[06:00] Evan M: noted — routing policy can be per-route. we'll include that in the runbook.
[06:06] Tom A: for DPA, minimal retention for logs tied to user data — HarborPay needs 30 day deletion SLA after request; can Redwood support data deletion for tokens/kv?
[06:18] Priya S: yes, deletion APIs exist; for cached KV we can purge tenant caches and rotate keys. some edge cases with backups, we'll document.
[06:30] Jorge R: security questionnaire — is there an existing answered version we can review?
[06:36] Lena O: yes Redwood has a living security pack (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, ISO if available) I'll share the secure link after this call.
[06:47] Tom A: perfect. also would like to see an example SLA credits schedule; what is the remediation if p99 spikes?
[06:58] Evan M: standard enterprise SLA includes uptime targets and service credits for breaches; we can share sample schedule. for p99 spikes it's often treated in runbook as incident with SLO review.
[07:11] Hannah L: procurement also needs to confirm that the pilot can be scoped to 3 weeks and include a canary for 1 customer lane.
[07:20] Priya S: yes we recommend a 3-week pilot with canary runway week 1, load week 2, validation week 3. metrics: latency, errors, cost per 1M tokens.
[07:33] Maya C: what about model version pinning during pilot? we want consistent outputs for QA.
[07:40] Priya S: you can pin model versions per-route; we'll lock the model for the pilot and allow controlled rollouts later.
[07:48] Tom A: on indemnity, our legal is asking for mutual indemnification for IP. is that standard?
[07:56] Evan M: Redwood's standard is mutual IP indemnity with procedure; we'll check but that's usually acceptable with reasonable limits.
[08:06] Marcus Y: circling to pricing examples — we've seen harbor-like customers move to Dedicated around 100–200M tokens a month. committed capacity gives predictability and lower marginal cost.
[08:21] Hannah L: ok if you can show the math for 200M tokens and for hosted vs dedicated that will help budget approvals.
[08:31] Evan M: we'll deliver a pro-forma with run-rate and worst/best cases.
[08:35] Tom A: any concerns about tenant isolation if we do dedicated?
[08:41] Priya S: Dedicated gives strong isolation (tenant pools), plus VPC peering to keep network traffic internal. On-prem gives maximal isolation.
[08:51] Jorge R: final question from me: key rotation and HSM audit — we need to see rotation schedule and proof of keys never exported.
[08:59] Priya S: we support BYOK and we'll document rotation policies; anything requiring non-export will be part of HSM integration spec.
[09:09] Evan M: ok quick recap: Evan to send MSA redline + term summary; Priya send perf/cost sheet and architecture diagram incl KMS/HSM flow; Lena to share security pack link and onboarding checklist; Jorge to send any non-standard compliance items. plan to reconvene after customers review the redline — target 2025-07-31 for signoff meeting.
[09:34] Tom A: thanks everyone we appreciate the clear path.
[09:39] Maya C: we'll prepare prompt set and QPS examples and share with Priya.
[09:44] Evan M: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links.

Meeting end.
